title: Last Bell, 2018
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: The bell. Gully's girl, eight, out of second grade. She asks Wood if he went to that school. He says he never left it.

panels.composition: Small Wood High, 3:05 PM, the bell. GULLY's flatbed at the curb — he's picking his girl up from the elementary next door. WOOD in the passenger seat with BARNABY II. The girl climbing in.

image.prompt: a flatbed truck at the curb of a small-town school at the last bell, a stocky man driving, a thin man in the passenger seat with a three-legged dog, a small girl climbing in, clean ink

balloons.text: Did you go to the big school?

image.prompt: close-up of a small girl in a truck cab between two men asking a question

panels.composition: Gully, driving, eyes on the road.

balloons.text: He means that in a bad way and a good way.

image.prompt: close-up of a stocky man driving with his eyes on the road, answering sideways

panels.composition: The flatbed pulling away, the school in the mirror, the bell shape fading. The girl's face in the back window looking at the school like it's already a memory.

image.prompt: a flatbed truck pulling away from a school with a small girl looking back through the rear window, the school small in the mirror, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: 'I never left it.' 'Ask him in twenty years.'
